chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: “At the canonical instance rate (~$20/hr per 8×H100 host), the canonical 6–21-host fleet on the owned/self-host basis is roughly $87.6K–$306.6K/month”
issue: Cross-chapter cost-basis inconsistency. The $87.6K figure is the 6-host cloud paid-occupancy line and $306.6K is the 21-host cloud always-on line in the §4.3 sidebar (pages 70–72). The self-host 21-host line in that same sidebar is $155,816.93/month. Labeling the cloud range as “owned/self-host basis” contradicts the earlier table and misstates the cost basis.
fix_instruction: Replace “owned/self-host basis” with the correct basis, e.g. “cloud paid-occupancy / cloud always-on basis,” or restate the self-host range using the $155,816.93 self-host 21-host line and the corresponding self-host 6-host line. Ensure the per-1K figures are also named to the matching basis.

chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: “Self-host cost per million input-only / output-only tokens … ($120/hr whole-fleet at ~6 hosts) ÷ (92,000 input tok/s × 3600 s/hr) → ~$0.362/1M input …”
issue: The cost-basis table labels the $120/hr whole-fleet calculation as “Self-host cost,” but $120/hr is six hosts at the $20/hr on-demand cloud rental price. In the same chapter, “self-host” is priced separately with capex amortization and energy ($155,816.93/month for 21 hosts). This is a provenance/cost-basis label mismatch that can mislead procurement comparisons.
fix_instruction: Relabel the table row as “Cloud on-demand rental cost per million tokens” or recompute the row using the chapter’s self-host capex/energy basis. Do not use “self-host” for the $20/hr on-demand rental basis.

chapter: Chapter 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
evidence: “For reference, the 9.5K total at this byte-halving basis is ~152 GB — still above a single H100, but now within 2×H100, 160 GB.”
issue: This aggregate-capacity statement can be misread as a fit verdict. The chapter’s own per-rank test for 2×H100 fails: each rank would hold ~70 GB of weights + ~6.225 GB of FP8 KV + ~32 GB reserve = ~108.2 GB > 80 GB. Saying “within 2×H100, 160 GB” without repeating the per-rank failure is inconsistent with the chapter’s three-gate fit discipline.
fix_instruction: Add “aggregate only” and state that the per-rank test still fails on 2×H100 at the stated reserve, or remove the “within 2×H100” phrase. Reconcile with Table 7-1’s “Conditional Pass” language.

evidence: "The ~50–60× envelope around that single geometry is the book's own characterization, not a figure from the report [1P][HYPOTHESIS]"
issue: Provenance label [1P] contradicts the sentence's own explicit statement. The Preface (p.15) defines [1P] as "first-party: the model vendor's own spec." The sentence says "the book's own characterization, not a figure from the report" — i.e. it is NOT from DeepSeek's spec. The provenance should be a book-internal tag (e.g. [ILLUSTRATIVE] or [2°] if interpreting published data), not [1P].
fix_instruction: Replace [1P][HYPOTHESIS] with [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] (or [2°][HYPOTHESIS] if treating it as interpretation of the cited second-hand source). The epistemic status [HYPOTHESIS] is correct; only the provenance axis is wrong.

evidence: "that occupancy and the canonical 8×H100 host definition are derived in Ch 4 §4.3 and Table 4-2"
issue: Cross-reference "Ch 4 §4.3" violates the reading convention stated on p.19: "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." The reference repeats the chapter number 4 in "§4.3" after already naming "Ch 4". Under the stated convention, "Ch 4 §4.3" would parse as Chapter 4, Section 4, Subsection 3 (i.e. §4.4.3), which does not exist; the intended target is Section 3 (= "4.3. Worked Example").
fix_instruction: Change "Ch 4 §4.3" to either "Ch 4 § 3" (chapter named, section stands alone) or "§4.3" (full form). Per the convention: "Ch. 7 § 3 means Ch. 7, Section 3" and "§ 7.3.1 is Ch. 7, Section 3, Subsection 1."

evidence: "ANALYTICAL (Axis 3, measurement status) — arithmetic on stated inputs (roofline, KV-residency and capacity screens, the C/W per-host bound and the host counts derived from it)"
issue: The Preface's evidence-discipline definition of ANALYTICAL references "the C/W per-host bound" using symbols C and W that are not defined until Chapter 4 (p.78: "C is reserved throughout the book for a host's KV slot capacity, C≈17.5" and W = mean time in system). A reader encountering an [ANALYTICAL] label in the body and returning to this Preface definition cannot understand the example without having already read Ch. 4.
fix_instruction: Either (a) add a brief inline gloss to the Preface: "the C/W per-host bound (C = per-host KV slot capacity, W = mean service time)" or (b) replace "the C/W per-host bound" with a self-contained phrase such as "the per-host capacity bound."

chapter: Ch 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
evidence: "At 9.2K tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — and the 8-bit raw byte-halving variant is ~12.06 GB — 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB, derived from the exact per-token byte count rather than the rounded 1.31 MB constant (the convention Ch. 7 follows); the 8-bit variant is not ~13.4 GB, because that is the overhead-inclusive estimate — 12.06 GB × 1.11 ≈ 13.39 GB, from adding an assumed ~11% block/metadata overhead to the raw tensor bytes (the ~11% is [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the 13.39 GB is [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED])"
issue: The 8-bit/FP8 KV figure is quoted at two different precisions in the same paragraph and across the book: 12.06 GB here (9,200 tokens, input-only) and 12.45 GB in Ch. 7 Table 7-1 ('FP8 total inference KV (9.5K max, resident basis) ≈ 12.45 GB'). Ch. 1's paragraph gives no indication that the 12.06 GB is the input-only basis, so a reader taking 'the 8-bit variant' as the per-request resident footprint understates the slot-counting figure that Ch. 7 and Ch. 17 use. Ch. 7 §7.3 explicitly names the two bases ('Per-request KV is quoted on two named bases: ~24.1 GB at the 9.2K input-only prefill ... and ~24.9 GB (byte-accurate 24.90368 GB) at the 9.5K input-plus-output resident slot'), but Ch. 1 does not name the basis of its 12.06 GB figure at all, creating an apparent 0.39 GB contradiction for the same '8-bit variant' of the same request.
fix_instruction: In Ch. 1's KV-cache paragraph, name the basis explicitly for the 8-bit figure: '~12.06 GB at the 9.2K input-only basis; ~12.45 GB on the 9.5K input-plus-output resident basis that Ch. 7 uses for slot counting', and cross-reference Ch. 7 §7.3 for the rounding convention. Apply the same basis-naming to the FP16 figure in the same sentence so the pair reads symmetrically.

chapter: Ch 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
evidence: "On the canonical 8×H100 host (TP = 8): prefill 1.29 PFLOP / (8 × 0.989 PFLOPS) = 0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION — the book's planning MFU, benchmark-informed: the [2°] industry range is 30–40%, and the 35% point is the book's chosen planning value, with 25/35/45% sensitivity in Ch. 8, Table 8-1]"
issue: The label attached to this row is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], but the value (0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU) is arithmetically derived from the canonical 1.29 PFLOP and the [1P][FACT] H100 peak; per the book's own Axis-2 rule in the Preface ('a value arithmetically derived from those assumed inputs ... is [canonical scenario][DERIVED]'), a computed time from canonical inputs must carry [DERIVED], not [ASSUMPTION]. Ch. 2's own Table 2-2 uses [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for exactly this class of number (e.g. 'Prefill: FLOPs, linear term only ... 1.29 PFLOP ... [canonical scenario][DERIVED]'). The ASSUMPTION/DERIVED split is explicitly the axis the Preface says is 'easy to get wrong' and 'is stated explicitly'.
fix_instruction: Split the label: the 35% MFU planning value is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]; the resulting 0.16 s / ~0.47 s prefill times are [canonical scenario][DERIVED]. Keep the MFU provenance in the derivation text and label the row's numeric result DERIVED.

chapter: Ch 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: "The minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline under the stated 35% MFU assumption is four, not eight: the 9.2K prefill is ≈1.29 PFLOP of work at 140 GFLOP/token, implying ≈1.19 PFLOPS of required compute rate over 1.08 s (9,200 × 140 GFLOP ÷ 1.08 s); one H100 sustains ~2,472 tok/s at 35% MFU, so a single GPU needs ~3.7 s for it (9,200 ÷ 2,472 = 3.72 s) and fails the cap, while ⌈1.19 PFLOPS ÷ (0.989 × 0.35)⌉ ≈ 4 GPUs meet it — the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s)"
issue: The 35% MFU planning value is used here to decide a hardware count ('the minimum GPU count ... is four'), but the Ch. 2 / Ch. 8 planning-MFU figure is explicitly a 'planning rate, not a ceiling' and the whole chapter labels analytical screens as 'not capacity results'. More seriously, the same paragraph's framing conflicts with the book's stated measurement discipline: Ch. 14 §14.4 and Ch. 8 require MFU to come from a benchmark, and the 35% figure is carried as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]. A 'minimum GPU count ... is four' derived from an assumed MFU is presented in the same sentence as a measured-sounding conclusion, and the 'four' number then reappears in Ch. 4 §4.8's mini-case host-count discussion ('the minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline ... is four, not eight') with the same status. The figure is analytically a lower bound (real MFU below 35% would require more), but the text states it as 'the minimum GPU count', which reads as a determined count.
fix_instruction: Re-label the four-GPU figure as an analytical lower bound conditional on the assumed 35% MFU — e.g. 'at the stated 35% MFU planning assumption the prefill deadline needs ≥4 GPUs; real MFU below 35% raises that count, so this is a floor to verify by benchmark, not a determined count' — and carry the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] MFU label with it wherever the 'four' recurs (Ch. 4 §4.8).

chapter: Ch 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
evidence: "That 8-bit figure is the raw tensor byte-halving of the FP16 value: 1.31 MB/token vs 2.62 MB/token, exactly 50%, with any block-allocation/metadata overhead NOT vendor-measured here and to be filled by a deployment benchmark."
issue: The '1.31 MB/token' rounding is used in a ratio claim ('exactly 50%') while the exact byte count is 1,310,720 B vs 2,621,440 B. 1.31/2.62 = 0.5000 exactly at the printed precision, so the ratio holds; however the same chapter prints '~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB) per token at 8-bit (~2.5 MiB, 2.62 MB at FP16)' earlier on page 31, and Ch. 7 states the canonical constant as '~2.62 MB (exactly 2.5 MiB/token)'. The dual-unit presentation (MiB and MB) for the same quantity — 2.5 MiB = 2.62 MB — is used repeatedly across Chs. 1, 3, 7, 17 and is the kind of quantity a reader will lift into a sizing slide; the book states the convention once (Ch. 1: 'MiB = 2^20 bytes and MB = 10^6 bytes') but Ch. 7's Table 7-1 mixes them inside a single row ('2 ×80 ×8192 ×2 B ≈ 2.62 MB = 2,560 KiB = 2.5 MiB'), where '2,560 KiB' is a third spelling of the same number and is not defined anywhere. This makes the load-bearing KV constant (which sets the entire fleet-sizing chain) hard to lift without ambiguity.
fix_instruction: Pick one unit for the KV constant across Chs. 1/3/7/17 (recommend MB, since the book's token-count convention is SI), state the conversion once, and remove the undefined '2,560 KiB' spelling from Table 7-1.

chapter: Ch 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: "Reference: one 8×H100 host (the ~$15,000 row) ~$14.6K — 730 h/mo" versus the sidebar's "Self-host — 21-host peak KV-screen fleet $155,816.93 ... 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff"

These two numbers are the entire basis of the self-host line item ($155,816.93), which the chapter then converts into '$24.97 per 1K requests' and compares against the cloud lines. Neither the $350K capex nor the $1,110.33 energy figure carries an evidence label or a derivation; Ch. 16 is where the TCO is developed, but the figure as presented in Ch. 4 reads as a computed total from unlabelled inputs, against the book's own rule that 'every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair'.
fix_instruction: Either move the self-host line out of Ch. 4 (leaving a pointer to Ch. 16) or attach the derivation and evidence labels for the $350K capex and the $1,110.33 energy term in place — stating the assumed PUE, host power draw, electricity price and amortisation horizon. If the values are canonical-scenario inputs, label them [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] and label the $155,816.93 total [canonical scenario][DERIVED].

chapter: Ch 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
evidence: "the capacity question — how many such hosts to absorb λ = 40 rps, where in-flight concurrency λ·W ≈ 344 at the ~8.6 s service time (that occupancy and the canonical 8×H100 host definition are derived in Ch 4 §4.3 and Table 4-2) — is answered later (Ch 16–17)"
issue: This cross-reference points the reader to 'Ch 4 §4.3 and Table 4-2' for the occupancy figure, but Table 4-2's 'Execution occupancy' row is the correct home, while Ch 4 §4.3 is titled 'Worked Example' and the occupancy derivation actually appears in the 'Arithmetic Walk-Through' subsection inside §4.3 (which the chapter does not number as a subsection) — so 'Ch 4 §4.3' does resolve to a section containing the arithmetic, but Table 4-2's occupancy row carries the value '~86 / ~344 requests' with the derivation 'Little's Law L = λ × Wexec'. The reference is therefore technically resolvable. The defect is that Ch 2 cites the occupancy and the 'canonical 8×H100 host definition' as being in Table 4-2, but the canonical host definition (8×H100, 640 GB) appears in Table 4-2's 'Hardware' row while the ~64 GB runtime reserve that the host's KV budget depends on does not appear in Table 4-2 at all — it is introduced in Ch 7 §7.1. A reader following Ch 2's pointer to validate the host definition will find an incomplete ledger.
fix_instruction: Either add the ~64 GB runtime/workspace reserve row to Table 4-2 (labelled [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], as Ch. 7 §7.1 labels it) so the canonical host definition is complete in the ledger Ch 2 points to, or amend Ch. 2's pointer to cite 'Ch. 4 §4.3, Table 4-2, and Ch. 7 §7.1' for the host definition.

chapter: Ch 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
evidence: "Table 5-2 — Model-selection decision: embedding vs generation model ... Verdict — embedding model: all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim) ... Selection status: recommended, pending target-corpus validation [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]"
issue: The embedding-model verdict carries [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] because it depends on the ~15% MAP uplift, which is an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]. But the verdict itself ('all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim)') is a selection decision derived from a table whose three rows are all [1P][FACT] model-card values (dimension, parameter count) plus [1P][DERIVED] FLOP proxies. The [ILLUSTRATIVE] provenance is applied to the verdict, which is a non-canonical scenario choice rather than a non-canonical worked example — the Preface's own Axis-1 note says '[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example: its inputs are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and its derived results [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', and separately that 'a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2), never [ILLUSTRATIVE] (Axis 1)' (Ch. 4 Note 1). The verdict row's status is a hypothesis about transfer to the target corpus, so it should carry [HYPOTHESIS] on the epistemic axis with the mixed-input provenance explained in prose, rather than being labelled as an ILLUSTRATIVE derivation.
fix_instruction: Relabel the 'Verdict — embedding model' row to the epistemic status that actually applies to an unvalidated recommendation (e.g. [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] or a mixed-input note plus [HYPOTHESIS]), and keep the mixed-input-provenance explanation in the derivation column, consistent with Ch. 4 Note 1's 'a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS], never [ILLUSTRATIVE]'.

chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
evidence: "Its language configuration has 16 full-attention layers, four KV-heads per layer, and a head dimension of 256 (released configuration, retrieved 2026-10-28). With BF16 KV storage, the raw component is: 2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 2 = 65,536 bytes per cached token. At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB."
issue: The arithmetic is internally correct (65,536 B/token × 262,144 tokens = 17,179,869,184 B = 16 GiB exactly), but the unit is stated in GiB while every other capacity figure in Ch. 7 is stated in decimal GB (the chapter locks the unit basis explicitly: 'the H100's quoted 80 GB is treated as decimal 80×10^9 B throughout, so the canonical 8×H100 pool reads 640 GB'). Mixing a GiB capacity into a chapter that has declared a decimal-GB basis, for a figure that is not itself a capacity gate, invites the reader to compare 16 GiB (17.18 GB) against the 640 GB decimal pool without the conversion. The same subsection then says 'At 131,072 tokens the same component is 8 GiB'.
fix_instruction: State the 16 GiB figure in the chapter's locked decimal basis (≈17.18 GB) or add an explicit parenthetical noting the binary unit and its decimal equivalent, so the figure is comparable to the 640 GB decimal pool used everywhere else in the chapter.

evidence: Page 31, Table 'Family... Bytes/token' row 'Reduced-width per-token'. Derivation: 'for full MHA: 2·n_h·d_h = 2×128×128 = 32,768'. Comparison: 'for MLA: d_c + d_h^R = 512+64 = 576'. Ratio claim: 'so 32,768/576 ≈ 56.9 ≈ 57×'.
issue: Arithmetic Error / Unit Mismatch. The 'Full MHA' value (32,768) includes a factor of 2 for K and V tensors ($2 \times n_h \times d_h$), whereas the 'MLA' value (576) appears to be a single concatenated latent vector ($d_c + d_h^R$) missing the factor of 2. If MLA stores both K and V latents, the correct denominator is 1,152, resulting in a ratio of ~28.5×, not 57×. The text compares a total storage metric against a per-tensor storage metric, inflating the efficiency claim by 2x.
fix_instruction: Re-evaluate the MLA geometry formula from DeepSeek-V2 paper. If $d_c + d_h^R$ represents the latent size for a single projection (e.g. key), multiply by 2 to get total KV state. Adjust the derived ratio (~28x vs ~57x) and correct the text's claim about KV cache shrinkage.
